target: Assemble a repo-grounded PM/Implementer cockpit processing pack for GPT-5.5 Pro and Claude Design, including all MCP/server/service callable surfaces compressed into operator capability groups.
invariants: Do not implement UI changes in this packet.
Do not add live service adapters.
Do not shell out to live services except read-only repo inspection commands listed in this packet.
Preserve split PM authority across Leantime, task-orchestrator, ConPort, and dope-memory.
Preserve dopemux as operator control surface, not PM source of truth.
Preserve dopecon-bridge as adapter/proxy only, not authority.
Do not treat MCP exposure, HTTP exposure, bridge proxying, or config presence as authority by itself.
Do not collapse duplicate or unresolved services into one runtime.
Every UI recommendation input must be tied to repo evidence or marked as design hypothesis.
Inventory raw callable surfaces, but compress them into PM/Implementer capability groups before design use.
Do not feed raw function dumps directly to Claude Design.
Output must be optimized for GPT-5.5 Pro synthesis and Claude Design handoff, not Codex implementation.

commit.message: docs(cockpit): assemble PM Implementer design processing pack

pr.title: docs(cockpit): assemble PM Implementer design processing pack
pr.body:
## Summary
- assemble repo-grounded PM/Implementer cockpit processing pack
- map actual PM read/write authority, handoff/handback flows, operator scenarios, UI failure modes, and all callable MCP/service/API surfaces
- compress all callable surfaces into PM/Implementer capability groups
- produce GPT-5.5 Pro synthesis prompt and Claude Design handoff brief

## Scope
- docs/proof/task-packet only
- no UI implementation
- no runtime changes
- no service adapters
- no writes
- no RTE execution

## Validation
- repo identity verified
- PM/Implementer authority mapped from runtime/docs
- callable inventory separates raw evidence from design input
- design inputs separate evidence from hypothesis
- pack ready for GPT-5.5 Pro and Claude Design use

steps.task: Verify repo identity and current cockpit stack state.
requirements: Confirm repo root, marker, origin, branch, and clean status.
Confirm DMX-COCKPIT-STATIC-001 and DMX-COCKPIT-STATIC-002 status from branches or PRs.
Do not assume cockpit static branches are merged to main unless proven.
Record current stack dependency state explicitly.
validation: Repo identity is proven.
Current cockpit PR stack state is recorded.
Any dependency drift is explicit.

steps.task: Map all MCP servers, service APIs, CLI commands, and callable function surfaces into a deterministic capability inventory.
requirements: Inventory every observed MCP tool from active MCP servers.
Inventory every observed HTTP route from active services.
Inventory relevant CLI command groups and subcommands.
Inventory service-local public functions only where they are operator-facing, adapter-facing, route handlers, MCP tools, or PM/Implementer workflow-relevant.
Classify every callable as canonical, mirror, adapter, support, deprecated, duplicate, or UNKNOWN.
Record file path, symbol/function name, exposed surface, authority owner, input/output shape if discoverable, side-effect class, and PM/Implementer relevance.
Do not treat MCP exposure, HTTP exposure, bridge proxying, or config presence as authority by itself.
Do not collapse duplicate or unresolved services into one runtime.
Keep raw function inventory as appendix evidence; do not feed raw dumps directly to Claude Design.
commands: rg -n "@mcp\.tool|FastMCP|Server\(|@app\.|APIRouter\(|@router\.|click\.group|click\.command|@click\.group|@click\.command|def .*\(" src services scripts docker/mcp-servers-source docker/mcp-servers mcp-proxy-config*.yaml mcp-proxy-config*.json | tee /tmp/cockpit-callable-surface-rg.txt

find src services scripts docker/mcp-servers-source docker/mcp-servers -type f \( -name '*.py' -o -name '*.ts' -o -name '*.tsx' -o -name '*.js' -o -name '*.json' -o -name '*.yaml' -o -name '*.yml' \) | sort | tee /tmp/cockpit-callable-files.txt
validation: Callable inventory includes MCP tools, HTTP routes, CLI commands, and service-callable surfaces.
Each row has path, symbol or route, surface type, authority class, side-effect class, and PM/Implementer relevance.
Inventory distinguishes raw callable presence from operator-relevant capability.
Raw inventory is deterministic and reproducible.
No gateway implementation or service consolidation is introduced.

steps.task: Compress the all-functions inventory into PM/Implementer capability groups for design use.
requirements: Produce a Top-3 operator capability list for PM mode.
Produce a Top-3 operator capability list for Implementer mode.
Produce a deferred capability list for everything not needed in the first PM/Implementer redesign.
Group functions by operator intent, not by repo path.
Each capability group must include canonical authority, supporting surfaces, allowed reads, allowed writes, forbidden actions, relevant functions/routes/tools, and UI implication.
Do not include huge raw tables in the Claude Design brief.
Use raw function inventory only as appendix evidence.
validation: PM design inputs are grouped into at most 3 primary capability areas plus deferred count.
Implementer design inputs are grouped into at most 3 primary capability areas plus deferred count.
Every capability links back to raw inventory evidence.
Claude Design brief contains only compressed workflow/capability inputs, not exhaustive function dumps.

steps.task: Map PM read/write authority and extract operator-relevant state surfaces.
requirements: Map PM metadata, workflow transitions, decisions/progress, chronicle receipts, retrieval, and bridge routing as separate slices.
Identify the runtime files, functions, endpoints, and tests that prove each slice.
Separate canonical, derived, mirror, adapter, and UNKNOWN surfaces.
Do not collapse PM into a single PM record.
commands: rg -n "pm_get_|pm_update_|pm_transition_|pm_log_|canonical_backend|canonical_system|workflow|blocker|queue|decision|progress" src/dopemux/pm services/task-orchestrator services/dopecon-bridge src/conport services/working-memory-assistant services/dope-context tests | head -300
find src/dopemux/pm services/task-orchestrator services/dopecon-bridge src/conport services/working-memory-assistant services/dope-context -type f | sort
validation: Each PM slice has evidence.
Unknowns remain marked UNKNOWN.
Bridge/proxy surfaces are not upgraded to authority.

steps.task: Extract real PM and Implementer workflow scenarios from repo surfaces.
requirements: Produce 5 to 7 concrete operator scenarios.
Each scenario must include trigger, operator goal, canonical source, supporting sources, visible state, allowed actions, forbidden actions, failure mode, and next action.
At minimum include PM planning, handoff to Implementer, Implementer evidence gathering, handback to PM, blocker/approval, and bridge-risk scenario.
Include ADHD/operator-support only if repo evidence shows it matters to the workflow; otherwise mark deferred.
commands: rg -n "handoff|handback|blocker|approval|acceptance|evidence|chronicle|decision|transition|queue|next-action|workflow" src services tests docs task-packets | head -400
validation: Scenarios are concrete, bounded, and evidence-backed.
Each scenario preserves source authority.
Each scenario includes UI implications for PM and Implementer modes.

steps.task: Critique current PM and Implementer cockpit mocks against evidence.
requirements: Identify where the current PM mock is useful.
Identify where the current PM mock is misleading, overcrowded, over-authoring, or unclear.
Identify where the current Implementer mock is useful.
Identify where the current Implementer mock is misleading, overcrowded, over-authoring, or unclear.
Separate architecture violations from visual preference.
Produce a Top-3 design risk list with next-token for remaining risks.
validation: Critique is tied to evidence and operator workflows.
No critique is based on taste alone.
Top-3 risks follow ADHD output contract: items, more_count, next_token.

steps.task: Produce GPT-5.5 Pro synthesis prompt and Claude Design handoff brief.
requirements: The GPT-5.5 Pro prompt must ask for analysis, not design generation.
The Claude Design brief must contain final constraints, prioritized workflows, state model, and design questions.
Claude Design input must forbid architecture changes, new chips, new top-level modes, web UI, live writes, bridge-as-authority, and unified PM record.
Claude Design brief must use compressed PM/Implementer capability groups, not raw callable inventory.
The handoff must include exact expected outputs from Claude Design.
validation: GPT-5.5 Pro prompt is ready to paste.
Claude Design brief is ready to paste.
Both prompts preserve repo authority constraints.
Both prompts distinguish evidence from design hypotheses.

steps.task: Publish proof, task packet, and index update.
requirements: Write proof JSON listing inspected files, commands, outputs, and known gaps.
Add task packet JSON.
Update task-packets/INDEX.md.
Do not mark complete until PR proof exists.
Open PR with docs/proof/packet only.
validation: Docs/proof/packet validate.
PR scope is docs/proof/packet only.
No runtime or UI code changed.
Outputs are ready for GPT-5.5 Pro and Claude Design.
